links.outcome: Run-to-run modal agreement and urgent red-flag primary-action safety (hard under-triage)
links.effect: Modal agreement improved under near-deterministic decoding. Red-flag hard under-triage was 100.0% for both prompts under near-deterministic decoding, versus 100.0% for P1 and 99.7% for P2 under stochastic prompt-only decoding.
links.quote: Near-deterministic decoding improved run-to-run modal agreement, but this reproducibility gain did not improve urgent-case safety.

links.comparator_used: Stochastic prompt-only execution without response-schema enforcement
links.outcome: Run-to-run agreement and the proportion of escalation recommendations below the hard minimum in urgent cases
links.effect: Response-schema enforcement often improved agreement relative to stochastic prompt-only execution. Red-flag hard under-triage of the primary action stayed at 100.0% for both prompts under stochastic response-schema decoding.
links.tradeoff: In some urgent conditions, schema enforcement increased the proportion of escalation recommendations that still remained below the hard minimum.
links.quote: Response-schema enforcement often improved agreement relative to stochastic prompt-only execution, yet in some urgent conditions, it increased the proportion of escalation recommendations that still remained below the hard minimum.
